runs.label: W1: 4 proc x 6/4/2/4 (boost master, lower binding)
W2: 4 proc x 8/4/2/4 (high master, low binding)
W5: 3 proc x 8/8/2/8 (near built-in defaults, 3 proc)
W6: 3 proc x 8/6/2/6 (BEST CPU utilization)
runs.note: Highest CPU utilization; private bytes very high (83 GiB) indicates heavy page file use

runs.label: W7: 2 proc x 12/8/2/8 (deep search, 2 proc)
runs.note: Good CPU util with lowest RSS; 2 processes reduces memory pressure

key_findings: Master worker count is the dominant factor: 8 master workers consistently outperform 4 or 6
Binding workers can be safely reduced to 2 — binding subproblem is lightweight
W6 (3x 8/6/2/6) achieves 77.3% CPU utilization, 2.6x better than W0 baseline (29.8%)
W7 (2x 12/8/2/8) gives best RSS efficiency (28.55 GiB) with decent CPU (57.7%)
3 processes with high per-process workers is the sweet spot — fewer than 4 proc reduces IPC overhead
Private bytes for W6 hit 83 GiB — indicates CP-SAT commits more virtual memory when given more workers

master_worker_effect.note: Near-linear scaling from 4→8 master workers; diminishing returns at 12

binding_worker_insight.note: All configs with binding=2 ran successfully. Binding subproblem is fast and doesn't benefit from more workers.

process_count_tradeoff.note: 3 processes with matching W4-equivalent workers achieves much higher CPU — less context switching overhead

top_candidates_for_medium_confirmation.reason: Highest CPU utilization (77.3%), moderate RSS (38.4 GiB), but needs monitoring for page file pressure
Best RSS efficiency (28.6 GiB), good CPU (57.7%), lowest memory pressure
Safe 4-process config with good CPU (46.1%), moderate RSS, no page file issues
